text: Good quality rice seed (រោប់ពូជសុទ្ធល្អ) should meet these characteristics: high varietal purity, not mixed with other rice varieties or weedy rice; free of disease and insect damage; grain and husk are clean, without cracks or chips; germination rate above 85%, with vigorous seedling growth; moisture content around 12-14%; weed seed contamination no more than 2%; and grains are full, uniform in size, length, shape, and color, true to the original variety's characteristics. Using clean, quality seed instead of ordinary saved seed brings several benefits: it can raise rice yield by roughly 5-20%; it lets farmers use less seed per hectare since germination is higher and more even; seedlings emerge more uniformly and grow more vigorously; the crop stand is more even from planting through maturity; plants grow faster and resist pests and disease better; the crop matures more evenly, making harvest timing easier to judge; milled rice quality is higher because it isn't mixed with other varieties or broken/weedy grain; and farmers can sell their paddy at a better market price.
